exact_statement: In the actual opposite-orientation priority gate selecting independent u and v when x=0,a=1 and x=1,b=1, respectively, and otherwise +1, let u=(-1,-1,-1,+1) and expose its first essential data bit at 0. For every nonconstant remaining Boolean v, let m=(1+Ev)/2. At the next private a query the owned selector rarity release kappa is zero, the source-compatible residual-product reference predicts both outcomes with probability 1/2, and its signed Bayes reset rho=JS-Gamma is strictly positive for all 0<m<1, with the exact scalar formula in PROOF (2). For v=(-1,+1,+1,+1), rho=2+(21/32)log2(7)-(25/16)log2(5) lies strictly between 21/100 and 43/200 bits. At this same actual root the canonical weighted occupancy credit v_nonempty K_occ exceeds L=(55/64)(10/7)(M0+M0^2/2)>43/200>rho, M0=1559232/9150625, proved by one excluded spectral event. The actual terminal child entropy average is 6-(49/32)log2(7)>17/10; root influence is 11/8 and query influence 1/2. Thus the proposed zero-price replacement rho<=kappa fails, while canonical occupancy credit quantitatively dominates this explicit reset debt at this fixture. No universal ownership, occupancy-change sign or full terminal payment is asserted.
